newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks up 4.25 pct by lunch on market support.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks up 4.25 pct by lunch on market support.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied 4.25 percent with the market index rising above its key 600 level by the lunch break after a small portion of a 50 billion baht market support fund was reportedly used for buying blue-chip stocks, brokers said on Wednesday. "I've heard that Krung Thai Bank, the administrator of the support fund, started investing about one billion baht in the market this morning," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
The composite SET index gained 24.53 points to 601.63 on 3.6 billion baht half-day turnover.
Krung Thai Bank declined to confirm that the support fund started buying on Wednesday but said it could begin tapping the fund from today.

"According to the Thai Bankers Association's resolution, one billion would be made available on Thursday but Krung Thai Bank is allowed to start buying today. We can place orders now and settle up to three working days later," Krung Thai Bank Senior Vice President Dusit Tengniyom told Reuters.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Saturday that commercial banks volunteered to pool 50 billion baht to help shore up the battered market.
Brokers said a U.S. Federal Reserve Board decision not to raise interest rates also helped boost sentiment after the Thai bourse lost 15 percent in the first half of this month.
All key sectors advanced. Banks led the rally, rising 6.28 percent, the finance sector advanced 7.08 percent, and the communications sector surged 5.40 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising eight baht to 158, TelecomAsia added 1.25 to 33.50, and Asia Credit rose 7.50 to 84.
